title: Leads Weekly Cadence — Sprint Showcase & Risk Triage (2026-06-24)
body:
Meeting: Leads weekly cadence — sprint showcase + risk triage
Date: 2026-06-24 10:00–11:15 PT
Location: Zoom + #eng-platform-leads
Attendees: Priya Nair (owner), Ethan Morales, Sofia Patel, Daniel Kim, Rachel O'Connor, Luca Moretti, guests: Maya (SRE), Anjali (Serving Runtime PM)

Agenda (timeboxed):
- 10m: Quick metrics snapshot and wins
- 25m: Sprint showcase (3 short demos / highlights)
- 20m: Risk triage (latency/regression + rollout policy concerns)
- 10m: Operations flags and upcoming changes affecting Dedicated/Private customers
- 10m: Actions, owners, parking lot

Quick metrics snapshot (Priya)
- 99th P50/P95 token latency for hosted-api: P50 stable at 80ms per token, P95 increased from 220ms -> 290ms week-over-week for long-context traffic (>4k).
- Token cost trending down 6% where batching applied; cache hit rate improvement on prefix caching to 32% globally (goal 40%).
- Dedicated pool utilization: avg 68% across GPU pools; burst capacity events handled successfully (no customer-visible errors).
- Incident summary: 1 Sev2 last Tuesday (RW-3245) — degraded throughput on pool B during autoscaling; mitigations applied and postmortem in progress.

Sprint showcase (high-level demos / notes)
1) Observability: Per-route tail-latency waterfall (Sofia)
   - Demo: new tracing view that associates token-level latency with kernel selection, batching decisions, and prefix-cache hits.
   - Early finding: slow tails correlate with GPU kernel selection fallback to generic matmul for certain sequence lengths; leads to 10–40% added token latency.
   - Ask: instrumentation to tag kernel selection in logs for 2 weeks (Action: Sofia, due 2026-07-02).

2) Serving runtime: Adaptive canary policy (Daniel)
   - Small canary runs for quantized variants now auto-expand based on error budget and token divergence metrics (alpha).
   - Result: one rollout aborted yesterday due to 0.8% perplexity drift on a customer eval set — auto-rollback kicked in.
   - Decision: extend canary window to 30 minutes for models with >8k param size to catch slow regressions (agreed). (Action: Daniel to update rollout policy, due 2026-06-30).

3) Private Deployments / Networking: VPC egress tuning (Rachel)
   - POC reduced cross-region chatter for control-plane heartbeats by batching config updates; estimated 18% lower control-plane CPU usage on private CPs.
   - Flag: some customers on older K8s versions need manual patch; outreach planned. (Action: Rachel + Solutions Eng to contact affected customers by 2026-07-01).

Risk triage (deep dive)
- Primary risk: rising P95 token latency on long-context workloads impacting SLAs for a handful of hosted API customers.
- Data points: spike correlates with increased traffic from a new retail customer sending long prompt chains during region-event peaks. Prefix-cache hit rate for those flows is low (~6%).
- Hypotheses: (A) kernel fallback for certain attention patterns; (B) batching policy not adapting to long-seq tails; (C) cache invalidation behavior for user-specific prefixes.
- Immediate mitigations discussed:
   1) Temporary traffic steering for that customer to a lower-utilized GPU pool with tuned kernels (SRE/Platform) — short-term relief. (Action: Maya + Ethan, run traffic shift 6/24–6/27, monitor).
   2) Increase aggressive KV cache TTL for hosted-api for sessions tagged as 'long-context-candidate' to try to boost hit rate (risk: extra memory). (Action: Priya + Daniel, evaluate memory impact by 6/26).
   3) Backfill kernel bugs: add metric export for kernel-fallback count, correlate with trace ids (Action: Sofia + Serving Runtime, 6/29).
- Escalation: if P95 does not drop 25% after traffic steering and cache tweak by 6/27, escalation to Exec + Customer Success for SLA messaging. (Trigger: P95 > 260ms persistently).

Operations flags / upcoming infra changes
- Autoscaling config change for Dedicated pools scheduled 2026-06-28 (non-disruptive) — will add 5% buffer to avoid thrash during region events. Solutions Eng notified.
- Storage upgrade for private deployment release v1.7 (on-prem package) will change disk layout; documented migration steps required. (Action: Rachel to publish migration doc by 6/30).

Decisions made
- Canary window extended to 30m for large models (>8k params). (Owner: Daniel)
- Short-term traffic-steering for the long-context high-traffic customer approved. (Owner: Maya + Ethan)
- Do not pause Dedicated autoscaling change — proceed but monitor closely for thrash. (Owner: SRE)

Action items (owner | due) — all owners to update Jira links
- Instrument kernel-selection tag into traces (Sofia | 2026-07-02) — add Jira link when created.
- Update canary rollout policy (Daniel | 2026-06-30) — attach policy diff to PR.
- Contact affected private-deployment customers for K8s patches (Rachel + Solutions Eng | 2026-07-01).
- Execute traffic steering and publish short report (Maya + Ethan | 2026-06-27).
- Evaluate KV cache TTL bump memory impact (Priya + Daniel | 2026-06-26).
- Finish postmortem RW-3245 and propose action plan for autoscaling edge-case (SRE lead | 2026-06-29).

Parking lot / follow-ups (non-blocking)
- Longer-term: explore kernel autotuning service that maps sequence-distributions to preferred kernels (research/eng partnership).
- Product ask: expose per-model canary thresholds in Console UI (Product + Console team to scope).
- Ops idea: trial a small ephemeral pool for long-context heavy customers (cost vs latency tradeoff analysis).

Notes to self / meeting cadence tweaks
- Keep showcases strictly 3 items max; demos should include 2-slide summary + 5m demo to stay within time.
- Add an explicit "customer impact" column to sprint showcase template so risks are visible up-front.

Next meeting: 2026-07-01 (same time). Priya to circulate pre-read by EOD Monday with updated metrics and RW-3245 postmortem link.

End of notes.
